title: PR #187: feat(rust): Ban shared-HMAC for web bot auth default verification
summary:
Per the protocol, shared HMAC is no longer considered acceptable for Web Bot Auth. Today, shared HMAC is not supported in keyrings, but may still have value for generic HTTP message signatures. Rather than prevent the use of the underlying HTTP message signatures library, we opt to make the Web Bot Auth verifier much stricter and enforce the contracts there.

This approach allows us to ensure full RFC 9421 coverage while also enforcing new Web Bot Auth requirements. The other approach - removing the algorithm altogether from `Algorithm` enum - would be a much more low-level breaking change.

title: PR #185: fix(caddy-plugin): address the remaining review findings from #167
summary:
@AkshatM, this takes care of the remaining findings from the review on #167: the code quality warning and the note about untested selection among several signatures.

## Signature-Agent members on httpsig-go v1.2.2

#167 made the example require a signature to cover the `Signature-Agent` member keyed to its label (Section 5.2.1 of `draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00`). httpsig-go v1.2.2 ignores the `key` parameter of a covered component and computes the signature base over the whole `Signature-Agent` field. As the review pointed out, a correctly signed request with a Dictionary `Signature-Agent` therefore gets `401`. The library fix is remitly-oss/httpsig-go#39, which isn't released yet, so this PR keeps v1.2.2 and documents the limitation.

- The README gets a "Known Limitations" section, and `coversSignatureAgent` gets a comment that states the limitation. Requests without `Signature-Agent`, or with a legacy String `Signature-Agent`, aren't affected.
- `TestValidateAcceptsIndependentlySignedSignatureAgentMember` signs a `Signature-Agent` member without httpsig-go. The existing tests sign and verify with the same library, so they pass even when both compute the same wrong base. The new test is skipped while `go.mod` pins v1.2.2 without a `replace` directive. It runs on any other version, so a dependency update, including a Dependabot one, fails it unless that version includes the fix.
- `TestSignatureAgentMemberBaseMatchesTestVector` checks the hand-built signature base against the ed25519 `Signature-Agent` vector in `packages/web-bot-auth/test/test_data/web_bot_auth_architecture_v2.json`, so the skipped test is known to be correct.
- The "covered member missing from `Signature-Agent`" case now changes `Signature-Agent` after signing. Before, it signed a member that the header lacks, which the fixed library refuses to do, so the case would have broken on the update. The case now also asserts that the request is rejected for the missing member.

title: PR #184: fix(web-bot-auth): write rsa-v1_5-sha256 as the alg of RsaV1_5Sha256
summary:
`Algorithm`'s `Display` writes `"rsa-pss-sha512"` for `RsaV1_5Sha256` ([keyring.rs L59](https://github.com/cloudflare/web-bot-auth/blob/f9584f30054ccbb0cb04e332e98199a64fa257a1/crates/web-bot-auth/src/keyring.rs#L59)), and `MessageSigner::generate_signature_headers_content` uses that string for the `alg` parameter ([message_signatures.rs L406](https://github.com/cloudflare/web-bot-auth/blob/f9584f30054ccbb0cb04e332e98199a64fa257a1/crates/web-bot-auth/src/message_signatures.rs#L406)). A `GenerateSignature` implementation that signs with RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 using SHA-256 ([RFC 9421 Section 3.3.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9421.html#section-3.3.2)) therefore gets a `Signature-Input` whose `alg` is `rsa-pss-sha512`. A verifier that checks `alg` against its key, as this crate does since #157, rejects it; one that takes the algorithm from `alg` verifies it as RSASSA-PSS with SHA-512, which fails.

The built-in signer for `[u8]` only implements `ed25519`, so this affects custom signers, which the `GenerateSignature` docs invite ("yubikey, cloud kms, web3 wallet", [L281-L284](https://github.com/cloudflare/web-bot-auth/blob/f9584f30054ccbb0cb04e332e98199a64fa257a1/crates/web-bot-auth/src/message_signatures.rs#L281-L284)). The `alg` parser already maps `"rsa-v1_5-sha256"` to `RsaV1_5Sha256` ([L61](https://github.com/cloudflare/web-bot-auth/blob/f9584f30054ccbb0cb04e332e98199a64fa257a1/crates/web-bot-auth/src/message_signatures.rs#L61)).

#### Changes

- `keyring.rs`: `RsaV1_5Sha256` displays as `rsa-v1_5-sha256`.
- `message_signatures.rs`: two tests. Every `Algorithm` value parses back to itself when its `Display` output is the `alg` parameter, and signing with a custom signer for `RsaV1_5Sha256` writes `alg="rsa-v1_5-sha256"`. Both fail on `main`.

title: PR #167: fix(caddy-plugin): apply the Web Bot Auth signature rules
summary:
The example accepted the first signature that verified, whatever its tag. It required only `created` and `keyid`, and didn't check that a signature covered the `Signature-Agent` header it was sent with.

This PR applies the following rules from `draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00`:

- Verify only signatures tagged `web-bot-auth` (Sections 5.2 and 5.4).
- Require `created`, `expires`, `keyid`, and `tag` (Section 5.2).
- When the request carries `Signature-Agent`, require the signature to cover the member keyed to its own label (Section 5.2.1). The signature can cover other labels' members as well (Section 5.2.2). A legacy String `Signature-Agent` counts as a single member keyed to the label, so the signature covers the whole field. The example rejects a value that is neither a Dictionary nor a String.

As before, the example accepts a request without `Signature-Agent`, because it loads its keys from configuration.

The PR adds no configuration and no network access. It keeps `remitly-oss/httpsig-go` v1.2.2.

Fixes #166.

## Tests

`go test ./...` passes, and `go vet`, `gofmt -l`, and `go mod tidy -diff` are clean. `TestValidateAppliesWebBotAuthRules` covers 11 cases:

- **Accepted:** a covered member, a covered legacy String, and a covered member alongside another label's member.
- **Rejected:** another tag, no `tag`, no `expires`, `Signature-Agent` not covered, a Dictionary covered as a whole field, only another label's member covered, a covered member that isn't in `Signature-Agent`, and a `Signature-Agent` that is neither a Dictionary nor a String.

The shared signing helper in `handler_test.go` adds `expires` and `tag="web-bot-auth"`, so the existing tests sign Web Bot Auth requests. Without the `handler.go` change, all eight rejection cases fail.

These tests sign with `httpsig-go` too, so the signer and the verifier compute the same signature base. They can't detect the `key` problem described in #166.
